items.entity: point force at mid-point of right edge
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says only 'an external force exerted on the middle point of its right edge'; the direction is shown only in Fig. 7. Sec. 4.2 says 'points downward' for a different cantilever (Fig. 14, 240x60), which suggests a vertical load. For a vertical load the sign does not matter: compliance and its sensitivities are quadratic in the load, so +y and -y give the same iterates, the same layout and the same compliance.
readings: vertical, pointing downward (-y)
vertical, pointing upward (+y)

items.entity: point force at mid-point of right edge
items.description: No force magnitude is given; Sec. 4 only says load data are dimensionless. A unit load is consistent with the reported C_ref = 92.7 and C = 92.8 (Table 3, 'Beam') at E = 1.
readings: |F| = 1 (unit nodal force)
|F| = 10 (compliance x100)

items.entity: void / minimum stiffness in the SIMP interpolation
items.description: Eq. (4) uses K_e = rho_e^p K_e^0 with only 0 < rho_e <= 1. No lower density bound or E_min is given anywhere (Sec. 2.2, Sec. 4).
readings: design-variable lower bound rho_min = 1e-3 (classic SIMP, E_void = 1e-9 at p = 3)
modified SIMP E = E_min + rho^p (E - E_min) with E_min = 1e-9

items.description: Sec. 4 gives only E = 1 and nu = 0.3. The paper never says plane stress or plane strain, the out-of-plane thickness, or the element formulation (it says only 'square elements', Sec. 2.1/4.2, Matlab code).
readings: plane stress, unit thickness, 4-node bilinear Q4 elements
plane strain, unit thickness, Q4 elements

items.description: Sec. 3.1 says thickness control 'can be achieved using the Heaviside filter [25], as will be demonstrated in Section 4'. Sec. 4.1.2 instead says thickness is controlled by 'direct usage of a density filter'. Sec. 2.3 uses a Heaviside projection only as a late black-and-white step. So the filter used during the main iterations is not fixed, and neither is whether the volume is measured on design or filtered/projected densities.
readings: linear (cone-weight) density filter with r_min = 1.5 throughout, with Heaviside projection added only later
Guest et al. (2004) Heaviside projection filter with r_min = 1.5 from the start
classic sensitivity filter with r_min = 1.5

items.description: The Fig. 7 caption sets the minimum thickness to 1.5, overriding the Sec. 4 default of 2; Table 3 confirms that 'Beam' equals 'Beam (r=1.5)'. Sec. 4.1.2 and Fig. 11 treat 'thickness' as the filter radius r_min, but 'thickness' can also mean minimum member width (= 2 x radius in a Heaviside length-scale sense). The unit is presumably element widths, since elements are 1x1.
readings: filter radius r_min = 1.5 element widths, centre-to-centre
minimum member width 1.5 elements, i.e. filter radius 0.75

items.description: Sec. 2.3 and Sec. 4.1.1 say a Guest-type Heaviside projection turns the gray design into a 0-1 design, but give no projection formula, beta value or continuation schedule, or threshold eta.
readings: Guest et al. (2004) form 1 - exp(-beta*rho) + rho*exp(-beta) with beta continuation, e.g. 1, 2, 4, ... up to 64
tanh threshold projection with eta = 0.5 and a fixed large beta (e.g. 32-64)

items.description: Sec. 2.3 says the black-white filter is applied 'in the last few steps'. Sec. 4.1.1 and Fig. 9 instead show it applied at step 45 (Fig. 9(b) to (c)) of a 166-step run, followed by about 120 more self-supporting iterations.
readings: switch projection on at about step 45, right after the relaxed-constraint phase, and keep it for the remaining iterations
apply projection only in the last few iterations before termination

items.description: Sec. 2.3 says only that problem (4) 'is ready-to-solve using the MMA approach'. It never confirms which update was used for the unconstrained/reference stage and the self-supporting stage, and gives no MMA or OC parameters (move limit, asymptotes).
readings: MMA (Svanberg) with standard parameters in all stages
OC update (move 0.2) for the unconstrained/reference stage, then MMA once the self-supporting constraint is added

items.description: The starting design is not stated. Sec. 4.1.1 says the volume fraction decreases during the iterations (Fig. 10(c)), which hints at a start above 0.6.
readings: uniform rho = 0.6 (the target volume fraction)
uniform rho = 1 (fully solid)

items.entity: termination and post-processing of the support-needed reference run
items.description: The reference design (Fig. 8(a); C_ref = 92.7 and 24 unsupported elements in Table 3) is obtained 'without considering' the self-supporting constraint. The text gives no convergence tolerance or iteration cap, and does not say whether densities are thresholded or projected to 0/1 before computing C_ref and counting unsupported elements.
readings: run to standard convergence (max density change < 0.01 or a cap of about 200-300 iterations) and evaluate the filtered gray design
same, then project or threshold to 0/1 (e.g. rho > 0.5) before computing C_ref and counting unsupported elements

items.entity: M_nd stopping threshold of the initial coarse (unconstrained) stage
items.description: Eq. (5) defines M_nd 'x 100%' (as a percentage) but sets M_nd^0 = 0.36, explained as the value for densities of 0.1 or 0.9 (4*0.1*0.9 = 0.36, i.e. 36%). Read literally, the threshold would be 0.36%. Fig. 9(a) shows a still-gray design at step 20 when the constraint is added, which fits 36%.
readings: stop the first stage when M_nd < 36% (0.36 as a fraction)
stop the first stage when M_nd < 0.36%

items.description: Sec. 2.3 says epsilon in U(rho) <= epsilon is 'decreased continuously from a relatively large value to the predefined tolerance epsilon_0'. It gives no start value, no epsilon_0 and no decrease rule or rate.
readings: start at U(rho) of the coarse design and decrease geometrically (e.g. x0.9 per iteration) to epsilon_0 = 1e-3
decrease linearly from a large value (e.g. 100) to epsilon_0 = 1 over the relaxed phase (about steps 20-44 in Fig. 9)

items.entity: density threshold for counting an element as supported (sign function, Eq. 8)
items.description: Sec. 3.2 says that for gray SIMP densities 'a specific value usually needs to be set to replace 0 in the sign function (8)', but never gives the value. It also does not say whether detection uses design, filtered or projected densities. With left-to-right printing, the supporting elements are the three in the previous column.
readings: supported if the summed density of the 3 supporting elements > 0.5
supported if the summed density > 0.1
supported if the summed density > 0.01

items.entity: final strict removal of the remaining unsupported elements
items.description: Sec. 2.3 says the remaining unsupported elements (at most 5) are removed in 'the last few iteration steps (when the number of unsupported elements is no longer decreasing)'. The trigger, whether removal is repeated, and whether optimization continues afterwards are not specified.
readings: set the remaining unsupported elements to void once their count stops decreasing, then stop
set them to void, fix them as passive void, and continue iterating to convergence
